title: Lifecycle rules and functions for an Auto Scaling group
scenario:
Your organization runs the `orders` job workers in the Auto Scaling group `orders-workers`. The configuration in `/home/coder/lab` creates the launch template `orders-worker`, the group, and the IAM role and instance profile of the workers. It has been applied.

Since the last apply, the scaling policy scaled the group from 2 to 4 instances outside Terraform. The application team has also delivered the boot script template `worker.sh.tftpl`, which should replace the static `bootstrap.sh`. The workers still have no security group of their own.

The folder is initialized. The `aws` CLI is configured for the account and region `us-east-1`.

tasks.text:
Stop Terraform from scaling `orders-workers` back to 2 instances.

- Add a `lifecycle` block with `ignore_changes = [desired_capacity]` to `aws_autoscaling_group.worker`.
- The group must keep its 4 instances and must not be replaced.

Hint: run `terraform plan` before and after the change. See [ignore_changes](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/meta-arguments/lifecycle#ignore_changes).
tasks.validation: Run `terraform plan`. It should not propose a change to `desired_capacity`, and `aws autoscaling describe-auto-scaling-groups --auto-scaling-group-names orders-workers` should show `DesiredCapacity` 4.

tasks.text:
Render the user data of the launch template from `worker.sh.tftpl`.

- Set `user_data = base64encode(templatefile("${path.module}/worker.sh.tftpl", { ... }))` and pass `environment` and `packages` from the variables.
- Make the group use the new launch template version: set `version = aws_launch_template.worker.latest_version` instead of `$Latest`.
- The launch template must not be replaced. Apply.

Hint: see the [templatefile function](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/functions/templatefile).
tasks.validation: Run `aws ec2 describe-launch-template-versions --launch-template-name orders-worker --versions '$Latest'` and decode `UserData` with `base64 -d`. It should contain `environment=prod` and one `yum install` line per package.

tasks.text:
Give the workers their own security group.

- Create `random_integer.suffix` with `min = 1000` and `max = 9999`.
- Create `aws_security_group.worker` named `orders-worker-<suffix>` in the default VPC, with `create_before_destroy = true`.
- Attach it to the launch template with `vpc_security_group_ids`. Apply.

Hint: a security group name must be unique, so `create_before_destroy` only works with a name that changes. See [create_before_destroy](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/meta-arguments/lifecycle#create_before_destroy) and [random_integer](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/random/latest/docs/resources/integer).
tasks.validation: Run `terraform plan -replace=aws_security_group.worker`. The plan should create the replacement security group before it destroys the old one.

tasks.text:
Allow every port in `var.worker_ports` from every CIDR in `var.trusted_cidrs`.

- Create `aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule.worker` (TCP) with `for_each` over all combinations, keyed `"<port>-<cidr>"` (for example `worker["8080-10.0.0.0/8"]`).
- Apply and finish with a clean plan.

Hint: `setproduct(var.worker_ports, var.trusted_cidrs)` returns all pairs; turn it into a map with a `for` expression. See [setproduct](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/functions/setproduct).
tasks.validation: Run `terraform state list`. It should list four `aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule.worker` instances, and `terraform plan` should report no changes.

tasks.text:
Reconcile `aws_autoscaling_group.worker` with how it is operated.

- The desired capacity is managed by autoscaling, not Terraform. It must stay at 4.
- The group must always use the newest version of `aws_launch_template.worker`, and a new version must show up in `terraform plan`.
- The group must only be created or updated after `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.worker`. Declare this dependency explicitly.
- The group must not be replaced.
tasks.validation: Run `terraform plan`. It should not propose a change to `desired_capacity`, and the group's launch template version in AWS should equal the latest version of `orders-worker`.

tasks.text:
Boot the workers with `worker.sh.tftpl` instead of `bootstrap.sh`.

- Render it with `environment` and `packages` from the variables.
- The launch template must not be replaced. Apply.
tasks.validation: Run `aws ec2 describe-launch-template-versions --launch-template-name orders-worker --versions '$Latest'`. The decoded `UserData` should contain `environment=prod` and one `yum install -y <package>` line per package.

tasks.text:
Create the security group of the workers and attach it to the launch template.

- `aws_security_group.worker`, named `orders-worker-<n>` in the default VPC, where `<n>` comes from `random_integer.suffix` (1000–9999).
- A replacement of the group must create the new group before the old one is destroyed.
- `aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule.worker`: one TCP rule per combination of `var.worker_ports` and `var.trusted_cidrs`, keyed `"<port>-<cidr>"`.
tasks.validation: Run `terraform plan -replace=aws_security_group.worker`. The new group should be created before the old one is destroyed. The group in AWS should have one ingress rule per port and CIDR.

tasks.text:
Add an optional canary instance.

- Declare `var.enable_canary` (`bool`, default `true`). `aws_instance.canary` must exist only when it is `true`; use `count`.
- AMI from `data.aws_ami.al2`, instance type `var.instance_type`, the first of the sorted default-VPC subnet IDs, and `aws_security_group.worker`.
- The canary must be replaced whenever the launch template gets a new version.
- Output `canary_private_ip`: the canary's private IP, or `null` when there is no canary.
- Apply.
tasks.validation: Run `terraform plan -var environment=staging`. It should replace `aws_instance.canary[0]`. `terraform plan -var enable_canary=false` should destroy it and set `canary_private_ip` to null.

tasks.text:
Reconcile `aws_autoscaling_group.worker` with how it is operated.

- Autoscaling owns the desired capacity, which must stay at 4. Raise `max_size` to 8.
- The group must use the newest launch template version, visible in `terraform plan`.
- The group must explicitly depend on `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.worker`.
- The group must not be replaced.
tasks.validation: Run `aws autoscaling describe-auto-scaling-groups --auto-scaling-group-names orders-workers`. It should show `DesiredCapacity` 4, `MaxSize` 8 and the latest launch template version.

tasks.text:
Boot the workers with the application team's `worker.sh.tftpl`, rendered with `environment` and `packages`.

- The rendered script must install each package on its own `yum install -y <package>` line.
- `bootstrap.sh` must no longer be used. The launch template must not be replaced.
tasks.validation: Decode the `UserData` of the latest `orders-worker` launch template version. It should contain `environment=prod` and one `yum install -y` line per package.

tasks.text:
Create the workers' security group `aws_security_group.worker` and attach it to the launch template.

- Name `orders-worker-<n>` with `<n>` from `random_integer.suffix` (1000–9999). Description `var.sg_description`. Default VPC.
- Changing `var.sg_description` replaces the group. When that happens, a new suffix must be generated and the new group must be created before the old one is destroyed.
- `aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule.worker`: one TCP rule per combination of `var.worker_ports` and `var.trusted_cidrs`, keyed `"<port>-<cidr>"`, except the keys in `var.excluded_rules`.
tasks.validation: Run `terraform plan -var 'sg_description=Orders workers v2'`. It should replace `random_integer.suffix` and create the new security group before destroying the old one.

tasks.text:
Add an optional canary instance and publish the rule keys.

- `var.enable_canary` (`bool`, default `true`) controls `aws_instance.canary` with `count`. AMI from `data.aws_ami.al2`, `var.instance_type`, the first sorted default-VPC subnet, `aws_security_group.worker`.
- The canary must be replaced whenever the launch template gets a new version.
- Outputs: `canary_private_ip` (`null` without a canary) and `worker_rule_keys` (sorted list of the ingress rule keys).
- Apply and finish with a clean plan.
tasks.validation: Run `terraform plan -var environment=staging`. It should replace `aws_instance.canary[0]`, and `terraform plan` without variables should report no changes.
